claims.claim: In 1948 Seán MacBride campaigned for a national target of planting 10,000 hectares of trees each year.
claims.episode_span: In 1948 Seán MacBride campaigned for a national target of planting 10,000 hectares of trees each year to create rural jobs and a domestic timber supply.
claims.source_title: Restoring bogs is more complex than just removing trees
claims.supporting_quote: At that time, about 2,400 hectares were planted annually. As minister for external affairs in the coalition government, MacBride introduced a policy of planting 10,000 hectares a year for 40 years

claims.claim: Peat soils account for 38.7% of Irish forests and forested blanket peatlands emit 1.68 t CO2/ha/year.
claims.episode_span: Dr Kenneth A. Byrne of the University of Limerick told the Joint Committee on Environment and Climate Action in November 2022 that peat soils make up 38.7 percent of Irish forests and that forested blanket peatlands emit 1.68 tonnes of CO2 per hectare per year.
claims.supporting_quote: peat soils account for 38.7% of forests

claims.claim: A 343-hectare Connemara plantation continuously emits up to 1,200 tonnes of carbon annually.
claims.episode_span: At the Connemara site the disturbed peat now emits up to 1,200 tonnes of carbon each year, according to measurements reported by The Irish Times in 2024.
claims.source_title: Restoring bogs is more complex than just removing trees
claims.supporting_quote: This Connemara plantation continuously emits up to 1,200 tonnes of carbon annually.
